messages.subject: barplot errorbars
parts:
Hello,
Ich made a barplot with errorbars, but the error bar do not appear in continuos lines for two of the bars, does anybody knows what I could do?

Br_bar<- ggplot(Brbar, aes(x=treat, y=BC)) + ylim(0, 1) + facet_grid(. ~ wm) 
Br_bar<- Br_bar + geom_bar(stat = "identity", width=0.7) + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=BC-Stdev, ymax=BC+Stdev), width=.2,
                                                                         position=position_dodge(.9)) + theme_bw()
Br_bar<- Br_bar + theme(text=element_text(family="Helvetica")) + theme(strip.text.x = element_text(size = 15)) +ylab("10^6 BrdU pos cells per ml") + xlab("Treatment")
Br_bar<- Br_bar + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size=15), axis.title.x = element_text(size=18),  axis.title.y = element_text(size=15)) + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size=15), axis.title.y = element_text(size=18))
Br_bar

thanks!
Inga

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: barplot errorbars
parts:
On 5/16/2014 8:09 AM, IRich wrote:
> Hello,
> Ich made a barplot with errorbars, but the error bar do not appear in
> continuos lines for two of the bars, does anybody knows what I could do?
>
> Br_bar<- ggplot(Brbar, aes(x=treat, y=BC)) + ylim(0, 1) + facet_grid(. ~
> wm)
> Br_bar<- Br_bar + geom_bar(stat = "identity", width=0.7) +
> geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=BC-Stdev, ymax=BC+Stdev), width=.2,
>
> position=position_dodge(.9)) + theme_bw()
> Br_bar<- Br_bar + theme(text=element_text(family="Helvetica")) +
> theme(strip.text.x = element_text(size = 15)) +ylab("10^6 BrdU pos cells
> per ml") + xlab("Treatment")
> Br_bar<- Br_bar + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size=15), axis.title.x =
> element_text(size=18), axis.title.y = element_text(size=15)) +
> theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size=15), axis.title.y =
> element_text(size=18))
> Br_bar

As Ben mentioned, without a reproducible example (including example
data), we can't say for sure. But I'll throw a wild guess out anyway.
You are limiting your y axis to between 0 and 1. I'm guessing that at
least one end of the missing error bars are outside that range. By
default, data outside the axis range is dropped, and if part of the
error bar is dropped, then none of it can be drawn.

As an aside, bar plots with error bars are not a great way to represent
data. Search for discussion of "dynamite plots" for further reading
about this.

> thanks!
> Inga
>

--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University
